newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan welcomes broad development in forex - MOF.
newsitem.headline: Japan welcomes broad development in forex - MOF.

text.p: Japan welcomes the "broad developments" in foreign exchange markets since the last Group of Seven finance ministers meeting, a Ministry of Finance official said on Thursday.

The official, speaking before International Monetary Fund (IMF), World Bank and G7 finance ministers meetings in Washington later this month, said that Japan would tell other countries at the meetings that its economy is on a gradual recovery path and would likely stress its own "urgent" need for fiscal consolidation.

The official said that broad developments in the forex market had been "stable" since spring and that U.S. monetary authorities had repeatedly said a strong dollar was in U.S. interests. "We, I think, welcome broad developments since the last G7 finance ministers meeting," he said.
On Japan's economy, the official said Tokyo hoped to tell other nations at the Washington meetings that Japan's economy was on a gradual recovery path.
"I think that the minister (Finance Minister Wataru Kubo) will stress the urgent need" for fiscal consolidation on both the expenditure and spending sides, he said.
U.S. officials have repeatedly expressed the desire to see Japan take the necessary fiscal and monetary steps to keep its recovery on track.

There have also been some signs that politicians, now gearing up for an election expected in October, would like to see some further stimulus in the form of an extra budget for the current fiscal year to March 1997, but the finance ministry, worried about Japan's bulging budget deficit, has been cool to the idea.
